action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is still to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is intact, and this kind of phase has historically been when spending to win new and returning users paid back best, especially among active traders. Apply it carefully for now: Bitcoin has been under its 50-day average for 18 days (about 7% below it) and is at its 30-day low, the mood reads fear at 28 out of 100, price is only about 4% above its 200-day average of $73,183, and Fed officials are talking about another rate rise before the 8 December meeting. So keep any increase small and easy to pause, lead with trust, safety and explainer messages, speed up only once price closes back above about $81,791, and pause the increase if price closes below $73,183. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, but the coming week looks soft. At about $75,823, Bitcoin is sitting on its 30-day low, has closed under its 50-day average for 18 days and is about 7% below it, and Fear & Greed reads 28 (fear); news is taking a little more off the week, as Fed official Mary Daly said rates may have to rise further (PANews). A normal week swings about $3,899, so a close above $77,750 (top of a typical week's swing) would turn it clearly up, a close below $73,183 (the 200-day average) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy. A calmer rate outlook would steady the week, while a close under $73,183 is the cue for safety-first messaging.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 19% higher and about 91% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 8% and about three people are betting on a rise for every one betting on a fall, which can make any further dip sharper. Price must win back $81,791 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there room to climb further; while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. The next Fed meeting is on 8 December, so keep bigger campaign pushes for a reclaim of the 50-day average.

The 3-6 month picture leans up at a moderate strength. Price is about 4% above its 200-day average, which is still rising about 5% over 90 days, while Bitcoin remains about 39% below its all-time high. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,183 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,699 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. Rule changes are a slow-moving factor here, with Bloomberg reporting that the new Democratic Congress means closer scrutiny (PANews); a close below the 200-day average is what would weaken this picture and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
